Two different questions. The whole work with EWS is relatively recent and Thunderbird worked fine for 20 or so years without EWS and is still doing everything I want using POP and IMAP, the open mail protocols.

If you are asking if Thunderbird will continue to support Microsoft proprietary protocols that story is a different thing. Thunderbird will migrate to something called the graph API by Microsoft prior to the EWS closure. Perhaps read the announcement/blog post https://blog.thunderbird.net/2026/09/thunderbird-desktop-new-protocol-support-microsoft-graph-api/

content:
Has anyone told you that using a VPN with a mail client often causes intermittent failures. Google in particular do not like you accessing their server via an VPN, other providers (mostly ISP mail providers) insist you connect to the internet to send mail on their service. You guessed it, having a VPN puts a cruel on that immediately by hiding your connection IP address.

So look for another mail client by all means, but I doubt you will be any happier with another until you tame whatever it is that is actually causing the connectivity problems and while Thunderbird is not fault free, I do not think it is to blame here. I would suggest the immediate problem is security software of some sort and most probably your VPN.

Qualsiasi pdf o solo alcuni? Inoltre, Per poter inquadrare il problema prova a fornire queste informazioni:

  1. Versione di Thunderbird
  2. Versione del sistema operativo
  3. Provider delle caselle email (Gmail, Libero, Hotmail, etc.)
  4. Tipologia di account (POP3, IMAP)
  5. Estensioni installate
  6. Messaggi di errore che vengono visualizzati durante l'utilizzo di Thunderbird
  7. Software di sicurezza eventualmente presenti (Antivirus e simili)
  8. Screenshot del problema (se utile a chiarire il contesto)
